title: Support Scoped Declarations
impact: 5 reactions plus a 'ran into the same issue' comment. @scope is Baseline (chrome 118, firefox 146, safari 17.4), and CSSNestedDeclarations ships in all engines (chrome 130, firefox 132, safari 18.2). Strict mode errors on valid CSS, and errorRecovery silently drops content: not only the declarations but sibling rules after them. That rises above a missing feature.
code: src/parser.rs: NestedRuleParser::parse_block, AtRulePrelude::Scope -> parse_style_block / parse_nested (allow_declarations is false at top level)
src/rules/scope.rs: ScopeRule (rules: CssRuleList; can hold CssRule::NestedDeclarations)
summary: css-cascade-6 allows declarations directly in @scope: "Contiguous runs of declarations are wrapped in nested declarations rules, which match the scoping root with zero specificity." At top level, Lightning CSS doesn't allow declarations in @scope. Strict mode errors ('Unexpected end of input' / 'Invalid token in pseudo element'). errorRecovery emits `@scope(.foo){}`, dropping both the declarations and a following `.a{color:red}` rule. @scope nested inside a style rule already accepts them, because of nesting. Implement it, with no flag: it's a stable resolution on a Baseline at-rule.
repro: 1165-repro.mjs. `@scope (.foo) { border: 1px solid black; }` -> strict: ERROR Unexpected end of input. `@scope (.foo) { border: 1px solid black; .a{color:red} }` errorRecovery -> `@scope(.foo){}` with the warning "Invalid token in pseudo element". Controls: rules-only @scope and `.x{@scope (.foo){color:red}}` work.
evidence: repro.mjs: identical on local, 1.33.0, 1.32.0, 1.31.1 (the issue's 1.31.1 screenshot matches). Chromium 153 probe: `@scope (.foo) { border: 1px solid black; .a{color:red} }` parses into a CSSNestedDeclarations child, and the border applies to .foo (1px). css-cascade-6 Overview.bs, section 'Scoped Declarations' (Status: ED). BCD 8.0.7 has no subfeature for scoped declarations. mozilla/standards-positions #1048 and WebKit/standards-positions #369 (Nested Declarations Rule) are both positive.

fix.approach: When parsing an @scope body, allow declarations (e.g. set allow_declarations in parse_nested for AtRulePrelude::Scope) and emit CssRule::NestedDeclarations. Keep contiguous runs in source order instead of hoisting all declarations to index 0 as parse_style_block does today: order matters against `:where(:scope){}` rules of equal specificity. Check that minify doesn't merge them across rules, and that nesting lowering of @scope inside a style rule doesn't change their meaning. Optionally, lower to `:where(:scope){...}` for targets with @scope but without nested declarations (chrome 118-129, safari 17.4-18.1). No JS AST shape change: only an existing union case appears in a new place.

subcases.item: related bug: nested @scope lowering drops the parent selector
subcases.status: separate, unfiled; `.x{@scope (.foo){.a{color:red}}}` with chrome 118 targets -> `@scope(.foo){:scope .a{color:red}}`, so the rule applies to every .foo instead of .foo inside .x (scope-start is relative to &). It only matters for targets with @scope but without nesting (chrome 118-119), so low. A case in the repro tracks it.

notVerified: Whether Firefox 146+ and Safari apply bare declarations in @scope. BCD has no subfeature, and wpt.fyi wasn't reachable. Both ship @scope and CSSNestedDeclarations, and the spec text is settled. I also didn't check how Chrome 118-129 treated these declarations, which matters for the optional lowering.
